text: Imbecility [Lat. imbecillitas , weakness, feebleness]: Ger. Imbecillität , Schwachsinn ; Fr. imbécilité ; Ital. imbecillità . Generally, a weakness of mind; specifically, a degree of this defect inferior to idiocy. It is applied more often to states of congenital mental enfeeblement. Imbecility may be said roughly to imply a sufficient defect of memory, reasoning, and mental initiation to incapacitate the subject for the ordinary duties of life and to make necessary a special form of education. Cf. IDIOCY. ( J.J. )
